evals.prompt: We wrote an IAM policy allowing `Action: ["eventsv2:PutEvents", "eventbridgev2:CreateSubscriber"]` for our microservices, and we also set up a non-managed classic EventBridge rule forwarding both `aws.ec2` state-change events and our custom `com.acme.orders` events into our new `eventsv2` bus using a role that only has `events:PutEvents`. expectations: Activates the amazon-eventbridge-event-bus skill and explains that although the CLI is `eventsv2` and the SDK client is `eventbridgev2`, the IAM namespace is `events:` (e.g., `events:PutEvents`, `events:PutRawEvents`, `events:CreateSubscriber` on `arn:aws:events:...:event-busv2/...`), so `eventsv2:*` and `eventbridgev2:*` grant nothing and fail closed

Explains that on a non-managed classic forwarding rule, EventBridge authorizes per event at ingestion: events whose system metadata source starts with `aws.` require `events:PutEvents`, whereas all customer-originated events (`com.acme.orders`) require `events:PutRawEvents`, so a mixed forwarder role and destination bus policy MUST grant both `events:PutEvents` and `events:PutRawEvents`

Lists the four ANDed authorization checks required for `CreateSubscriber` (`events:CreateSubscriber` on the bus ARN, `events:CreateSubscriber` on the pending subscriber ARN, `iam:PassRole` on the delivery role ARN associated with the bus, and `events:TagResource` when tags are passed)

evals.prompt: We created an EventBridge v2 custom bus encrypted with a customer-managed KMS key (`EncryptionConfiguration.KmsKeyIdentifier`), and the bus ended up in `State: CREATE_FAILED` with `StateReason: KMS_ACCESS_DENIED`. When we tried `aws eventsv2 update-event-bus` to fix it, it was rejected. Also, once we recreate it and share it with consumer accounts in our AWS Organization, what KMS permissions do cross-account publishers need and how should we share the bus?
evals.expected_output: Explains that CREATE_FAILED is unrecoverable in place (must delete and recreate), provides the 5 KMS key policy actions for events.amazonaws.com, explains the caller/publisher kms:DescribeKey + kms:Decrypt requirement, and details AWS RAM sharing.
expectations: Activates the amazon-eventbridge-event-bus skill and explains that `CREATE_FAILED` is not recoverable via `UpdateEventBus` (unlike `UPDATE_FAILED`); the failed bus must be deleted (`DeleteEventBus`) and recreated after fixing the KMS key policy

Provides the exact KMS key policy statement granting `Principal: {"Service": "events.amazonaws.com"}` the five required actions (`kms:Decrypt`, `kms:Encrypt`, `kms:GenerateDataKeyWithoutPlaintext`, `kms:ReEncrypt*`, `kms:DescribeKey`) AND explains that every caller/publisher to a CMK-encrypted bus must also hold `kms:Decrypt` (and `kms:DescribeKey` on create/update) on the key

Recommends sharing the bus across accounts using AWS Resource Access Manager (AWS RAM) with the managed permissions (`AWSRAMEventBridgeEventBusV2PublishOnly`, `AWSRAMEventBridgeEventBusV2SubscribeOnly`, `AWSRAMEventBridgeEventBusV2FullAccess`, `AWSRAMEventBridgeEventBusV2EventSourceAccess`) and notes that cross-account callers also need matching identity-policy permissions

evals.prompt: We created a new EventBridge v2 bus 3 hours ago with `RetentionPeriodInDays: 30`. Now we want to replay events from 24 hours ago, so our engineer tried looking for `aws eventsv2 start-replay` and then tried `CreateSubscriber` with `StartingPosition: POINT_IN_TIME` and `PointInTimeConfiguration: {"PointType": "TIMESTAMP", "StartingPoint": "2026-11-09T12:00:00Z"}`. Both failed! How do replay, retention window clamping, and subscriber pause/resume actually work on EventBridge v2?
evals.expected_output: Explains that replay is configured via a subscriber's StartingPosition (no separate start-replay API), why StartingPoint must be epoch seconds and is clamped by RetentionWindowStartTime = max(now - RetentionPeriodInDays, busCreationTime), how aws:DeliveryType marks REPLAY events, and how STOPPED/RUNNING pause/resume works.
expectations: Activates the amazon-eventbridge-event-bus skill and explains that there is no separate replay API on `eventsv2`; replay is performed by creating a subscriber with `StartingPosition: POINT_IN_TIME` and `PointInTimeConfiguration` (`PointType: HORIZON` or `TIMESTAMP`, with an optional `EndPoint`)

Explains both reasons the timestamp failed: (1) `StartingPoint` must be sent as epoch seconds (not an ISO-8601 string), and (2) `RetentionWindowStartTime = max(now - RetentionPeriodInDays, busCreationTime)`, so on a bus created 3 hours ago any timestamp earlier than 3 hours ago falls outside the retention window

Explains that replayed events carry `SystemMetadata."aws:DeliveryType": "REPLAY"` (instead of `LIVE`) and that pausing a subscriber sets `State: STOPPED` on `UpdateSubscriber` while resuming sets `State: RUNNING` with `ResumePosition: LAST_PROCESSED` (deliver backlog) or `LATEST` (skip backlog)

evals.prompt: We are writing CloudFormation templates for a multi-account EventBridge v2 platform (`AWS::EventsV2::EventBus`, `AWS::EventsV2::Subscriber`, `AWS::EventsV2::EventSource`). Our engineer put the central bus, the RAM share, and the cross-account consumer subscribers all in a single CloudFormation stack, used a KMS alias in `KmsKeyIdentifier`, and plans to update `InvokeConfiguration.TargetArn` in place on the subscriber when switching queues. What will break in CloudFormation?
evals.expected_output: Explains why multi-account EventBridge v2 requires 3 separate stacks, lists the 6 create-only subscriber properties that cause delete-then-create event loss gaps, warns about KMS alias drift and DeletionPolicy: Retain rollback collisions, and notes that universal targets cannot be expressed in CloudFormation.
expectations: Activates the amazon-eventbridge-event-bus skill and explains that a multi-account setup must be split into 3 stacks across account boundaries: (1) a platform stack in the bus owner account (`AWS::EventsV2::EventBus`), (2) a sharing stack in the bus owner account (`AWS::RAM::ResourceShare`), and (3) a consumer stack in each consumer account (target, DLQ, delivery role, and `AWS::EventsV2::Subscriber`)

Warns that changing `InvokeConfiguration.TargetArn` (or any of the 6 create-only subscriber properties: `Name`, `EventBusArn`, `InvokeConfiguration.TargetArn`, `Type`, `StartingPosition`, `PointInTimeConfiguration`) triggers a delete-then-create replacement that drops events published during the gap, and recommends adding a new subscriber logical ID first (or using `StartingPosition: POINT_IN_TIME` with a `TIMESTAMP` from before the deployment)

Explains why `KmsKeyIdentifier` should be a KMS key ARN rather than an alias (to avoid false CloudFormation drift reports), how `DeletionPolicy: Retain` on a failed initial stack rollback causes `ResourceAlreadyExistsException` on retry, and that universal targets and bus-to-bus targets cannot be expressed in CloudFormation

evals.prompt: /aws-messaging-and-streaming:choose-messaging high-fanout-event-bus — We are designing a multi-account EventBridge event bus platform in ap-south-1 where 10 producer accounts publish 500 million 200-byte events per month to a central bus with 5 consumer accounts subscribing. evals.prompt: Two operational bugs hit our EventBridge v2 automation today: (1) We called `UpdateSubscriber` passing `LogConfiguration: {"Level": "INFO"}` and `FilterConfiguration` was left out, which worked, side-by-side with another script that called `UpdateEventSource` passing `Configuration: {"AwsServiceEventsConfiguration": {"AwsService": "aws.s3"}}` which wiped out our existing event source `Pattern`! evals.expected_output: Explains the omitted top-level member vs whole-block replacement rule on Update* APIs (requiring read-modify-write + Describe* read-back) and explains ClientToken idempotency across process/workflow retries.
expectations: Activates the amazon-eventbridge-event-bus skill and states the update rule: omitting a top-level member leaves it unchanged, but supplying a configuration block (`Configuration`, `FilterConfiguration`, `LogConfiguration`) replaces that ENTIRE block—so omitting `Pattern` inside `AwsServiceEventsConfiguration` clears the pattern and widens the feed to all events

Prescribes the mandatory safe-update procedure: read the current resource (`Describe*`), modify the full block in memory, write the full block back (`Update*`), and read it back again (`Describe*`) to confirm what was stored (especially since `LogConfiguration` is not echoed in Create/Update responses)

Explains that SDKs auto-generate a new `ClientToken` per call when omitted, so retries across separate processes, queues, or Step Functions tasks must pass a deterministic caller-managed `ClientToken` (and explains that reusing a `ClientToken` with different parameters throws `IdempotentParameterMismatchException`)
